components.text: Most relevant to us: the August top-up lifts subsidized loans per firm to ¥75m

footnote: Source: policy documents from the State Council, MIIT and the Ministry of Finance, and State Council meeting releases (January–September 2026). Dates are publication dates
notes: This year's added policies run along two lines. Spending: in January the State Council issued a plan to grow new areas of services consumption, in July it approved a plan to expand consumption over 2026–2030 that aims for retail sales of about ¥60 trillion by 2030, and in August the Ministry of Finance and others raised the yearly cap on interest subsidies for personal consumer loans from ¥3,000 to ¥5,000 and the subsidized loan amount per small firm from ¥50 million to ¥75 million, effective August 1. Industry and jobs: in January the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and seven other agencies launched an AI Plus manufacturing action plan, and small and micro firms got a loan interest subsidy of 1.5 points a year for up to two years. In June the State Council issued a five-year employment-first plan. On September 28 a State Council executive meeting called for making good use of unused local government debt quota and more central bank relending for technology innovation and equipment upgrades.
